name: Barbell Bench Press
summary: The classic horizontal press for the chest, front delts and triceps. A staple for building upper-body pressing strength and muscle.
setup: Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar, feet flat on the floor under your knees.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down and keep them pinned to the bench; keep a small natural arch in the upper back.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with the bar low in the palm and wrists stacked over forearms.
Unrack with straight arms and settle the bar over the shoulders. Set the safety arms or use a spotter.
execution: Take a breath, brace your abs and lower the bar under control to the lower chest/sternum area, elbows about 45-70 degrees from the torso.
Touch the chest lightly without bouncing.
Press the bar back up and slightly toward the rack in a smooth path until the arms are straight.
Rack the bar only when the set is finished and the arms are locked out.
cues: Feet planted, push the floor away
Bend the bar in your hands, elbows tucked not flared
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest: lower with control and pause briefly on the chest.
Elbows flared to 90 degrees: tuck them to roughly 45-70 degrees to protect the shoulders.
Hips lifting off the bench: keep glutes down and drive through the feet instead.
Wrists bent back: stack the bar over the forearm with a firm grip.
